title: Choir and Spire
premise: In the valley of Hollowmere, where an ancient ward keeps magic out and its people safe, Vesper Vane has survived by being forgettable—the last apprentice of a guild that once sang the ward into being. When prayers across the valley begin receiving answers from something old and hungry, Vesper learns the ward is failing and the 'king' beyond the pass has been hollowed out and worn like a glove by a god that eats memory. To save her found family, she must leave the only home she's known, relearn the guild's forbidden songs, and unbind the king by offering her own memories as counterweight. In the end she defeats the god but pays with every recollection of the people she loves—returning to a valley full of strangers who call her family, forcing her to choose whether love can be rebuilt from nothing.
about_author: Bram Sterling is the pen name of a former cathedral chorister who spent a decade restoring medieval manuscripts before turning to fiction. They write about music, memory, and the quiet violence of small communities.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet Hollowmere through its rituals: the nightly bell, the silent guildhall, the ward-stones no one questions. Vesper tends the dying Master Aldous and hides her ability to hear the ward humming. Emotional beat: comfortable invisibility curdling into loneliness as she realizes she may be the last who understands what holds the valley together.

chapters.title: Answers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A neighbor's prayer for rain is answered overnight—and so is a child's prayer for his dead mother to return. The returned thing wears his mother's face imperfectly. The guild's records confirm: the ward is thinning. Emotional beat: dread; the safety of the valley revealed as a shrinking border, not a sanctuary.

chapters.title: What the Bell Remembers
chapters.summary: Master Aldous's POV in his final lucid hours. He tells Vesper the truth: the guild didn't build the ward, they bargained for it, and the price was paid in memories each generation. He dies mid-song, leaving her half a melody. Emotional beat: grief braided with inheritance; Vesper inherits a debt disguised as a gift.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, first journey past the ward-stones. Magic floods back into her senses painfully. She reaches the border town of Cairnlow and sees the king at a distance—moving wrong, smiling wrong, attended by answered-prayer creatures. Emotional beat: awe and horror; the wider world is both more beautiful and more damned than she imagined.

chapters.title: Found Company
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Tam, a disgraced royal archivist who recognized the king's hollowness and fled. Tam becomes her reluctant guide and first true friend. They decode the guild's half-melody as a binding song meant to be sung by two voices. Emotional beat: warmth; Vesper discovers companionship and hates how much she needs it.

chapters.title: The God That Eats Yesterday
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Research reveals the god Ourod feeds on memory, which is why it cannot enter the valley: there is nothing there for it to take—it was made deliberately bland. The king invited it in, trading his kingdom's past for protection from famine. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the enemy was invited, and the invitation was rational.

chapters.title: Choir of the Hollowed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Captured and brought to the capital, she finds the court: nobles with neatly excised pasts, contented and empty. The king, deep inside, still fights—his fragmentary self begs her through a children's rhyme he shouldn't remember. Emotional beat: pity sharpening into resolve; the enemy is also a prisoner.

chapters.title: Counterweight
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Escape and preparation. The binding requires two singers and a price: the song must be anchored in offered memories. Tam volunteers his own past, but the melody demands one voice that has never been touched by magic—only Vesper qualifies. Emotional beat: sacrifice contemplated honestly, without heroics; fear shared between friends.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, climax. Before the throne, she and Tam sing the completed song while the king's buried self rises to hold Ourod's attention. Vesper offers her memories of Hollowmere—her whole life—as anchor. The god unravels; the king collapses, freed and broken. Emotional beat: triumphant devastation; victory that costs exactly what it promised to cost.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Call Me Family
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, resolution. She returns to Hollowmere remembering nothing of it, yet her hands know the bell rope, her voice knows the songs. The valley greets her as kin. She begins again: learning names, keeping a journal, choosing these people daily. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope; memory lost, but love proven renewable—a found family chosen twice.
